title: Tiered graceful degradation with KV-cooling windows for SLO-compliant continuous batching
creator: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary:
We need a new SLO-aware degradation path for continuous batching that minimizes user-facing latency regressions while protecting GPU memory and KV cache health. The proposal introduces a tiered, time-windowed demotion model ("demotion grades") plus per-tenant bandwidth tokens and a KV-cooling window to reduce hard evictions and oscillation under contention.

Background / Motivation:
- Current continuous batching preemption is binary: either allow a request to proceed or preempt it/hard-evict KV state. This causes visible tail-latency spikes and repeated cache thrashing when contention is sustained.
- Many customer workloads are sensitive to sub-200ms tail latency SLOs and cannot tolerate frequent full-model re-warm that follows hard eviction.
- We need a mechanism that offers incremental de-escalation of resource usage, amortizes KV eviction, and enforces fair GPU memory use across tenants while respecting SLOs.

Goals:
1) Reduce tail-latency regressions for latency-sensitive tenants during sustained contention.
2) Prevent KV cache oscillation and repeated cold-start penalties by introducing a cooling window and soft demotion steps.
3) Provide per-tenant fairness guarantees expressed as soft bandwidth budgets and graceful degradation, not binary kills.
4) Keep per-request decision latency minimal (<500us extra on scheduling path).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change long-term eviction policies for cold-set compaction or persistent KV migration across nodes.

Proposal (high level):
1) Demotion grades: define 3 demotion grades (G0: full resources, G1: I/O-limited prefix-only slices + reduced KV residency, G2: heavily demoted: low-priority timeslices with strict token metering). Demotion happens incrementally: G0 -> G1 -> G2.
2) KV-cooling window: when a tenant has objects evicted due to memory pressure, mark those keys with a cooling TTL (e.g., 60s) during which we prefer soft demotion rather than re-eviction. The cooling window avoids immediate re-population thrash.
3) Soft reclaim tokens: allocate per-tenant reclaim tokens (bandwidth units) that are consumed when a request would cause additional KV residency or exceed per-tenant GPU memory fraction. Tokens replenish on a configurable cadence.
4) Speculative demotion: for long-running requests that would likely exceed SLOs, the scheduler can speculatively route remaining work to a demoted execution lane rather than abruptly preempting current slice; this reduces rollback and client retries.
5) Admission + telemetry: add metrics for demotion grade transitions, token consumption, cooling-window hits, and observed tail latency per tenant. Expose a console dashboard and slow-path tracer.

Design details:
- Scheduling path changes: extend continuous-batcher admission check to consult demotion state and token balance. Keep critical fast path checks simple (boolean flags + token lookup).
- Token accounting: tokens are integer counters with refill rate R per tenant. A request declares an expected KV-add delta (estimated via prefix length and model type); the scheduler pre-decrements tokens; if insufficient, it triggers next demotion grade.
- KV-cooling: when eviction occurs, write a soft-mark to in-memory key table (no disk I/O) with expiry timestamp. On subsequent evictions within window, prefer demotion step instead of evicting again.
- Implementation modules: new scheduler module DemotionManager, TokenBucket per-tenant, KV-Cooler co-located with KV index. Add small API hooks for runtime to mark demotion and to route to demoted execution lanes.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end demo where a noisy tenant causing >80% GPU memory pressure is de-escalated through G1/G2 and tail P99 latency for affected low-latency tenants improves by >=40% compared to current baseline under same load.
- Cooling window reduces repeated evictions for the same keys by >=60% in induced contention tests.
- Scheduler overhead added <500us median on scheduling decisions in microbenchmarks.
- Rollout toggles via feature-flag and per-tenant opt-in.

Tests / Validation:
- Unit tests for token accounting, demotion transitions, KV-cooling flag expiry.
- Integration test harness that replays mixed-tenancy traces (from internal replay corpus) and asserts latency and eviction metrics.
- Chaos test: long-running sustained overcommit with synthetic tenants to verify demotion avoids oscillation and keeps fairness allocations.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged implementation behind runtime-1.25.
2) Internal dogfood: enable for non-critical dev tenants for 1 week.
3) Canary: enable for 5% of production traffic on dedicated pools with observability.
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% after metric gates.

Risks / Tradeoffs:
- Mis-estimates of KV-add delta could cause over-demotion; mitigate by conservative estimates and telemetry-driven tuning.
- Token starvation could unfairly throttle small bursty tenants; we'll add burst allowances and emergency exception pathway.
- Complexity: adds three small coordination points (DemotionManager, TokenBucket, KV-Cooler) — keep interfaces minimal and well-tested.

Observability / Dashboard:
- New console tile: "Demotion heatmap" showing per-tenant grade distribution over time.
- Metrics: demotion_transitions_total, tokens_consumed_total, kv_cooling_hits_total, p99_latency_by_tenant.
- Tracing: attach scheduling decision metadata to request traces (grade before/after, token delta).

Open questions:
- Default cooling window length: 30s, 60s, or 120s? Start with 60s and tune.
- Token refill policy: uniform time-based vs. adaptive based on recent usage. Start uniform then consider adaptive.
- Interaction with existing preemption: can demoted lanes still be preempted? Proposal: demoted lanes are soft-preemptible but with lower priority; final hard-preempt still possible under emergency OOM.

updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on demotion grades and cooling window concept. Action: Priya to prototype in-memory cooling mark storage.

2026-02-18: Prototype notes — KV-cooler implemented in local branch; observed 45% reduction in repeated evictions on small synthetic workload. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4167
2026-02-25: Architecture review with SRE — requested clearer emergency OOM pathway and metric SLIs. Added emergency hard-preempt override to design.

2026-03-04: Demo to PM — showed workload demo with two tenants; tail latency for latency-sensitive tenant P99 improved by ~47% in the prototype. PM requested configurable per-tenant cooling window and console toggles.
2026-03-10: Implementation in progress — DemotionManager basic logic merged to feature branch. TokenBucket API landed. Next: add KV integration and end-to-end tests (see sub-issues).
